speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I have been preparing for a natural water birth and I DO NOT want a c-section.
context: Scan finding at 32 weeks makes a planned surgical birth likely; she feels robbed of her planned birth.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I can’t help but feel like I’ve been robbed of the birth I wanted. I feel like I’m losing yet another body autonomy for this pregnancy.
context: Weighing an elective surgical birth after a scan finding.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: when I asked about the cost/benefits, I was dismissed with “preeclampsia is bad, you don’t want preeclampsia.”
context: Her OB's answer when she questioned a prescribed medication.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Yes, the idea of recovering from surgery while trying to take care of a baby scares me.
context: Learned at 36 weeks the baby is head-up; never had surgery before.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m terrified of a c section. Any advice or positive stories. I’ve never had surgery. I can’t stop crying this is not what I wanted.
context: Post written the day she learned baby's position at 36 weeks.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I’ve had people tell me that a c-section was the best thing they ever had, while others tell me that the recovery is not worth it and to possibly try again with the vaginal birth if I can do it.
context: Choosing birth type for her second after a long, injurious first labour.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Then next thing I know, my algorithm starts bombaring me with all of this terrifying CMV stuff. It’s just so unfair and backwards.
context: A single TikTok about an infection sent her feed into a spiral at five weeks.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I miss having my body to myself. I want to be alone in my body… I miss being able to move normally, sleep comfortably, and not feel like I’m sharing every part of myself 24/7.
context: Overdue with her second baby.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I feel guilty even admitting it because I already love my baby so much (second pregnancy), but I’m just so physically and mentally exhausted.
context: Overdue; asks if wanting her body back is selfish.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I normally love summer because you can be outside, move around freely, and do so much. But being heavily pregnant during summer is a completely different experience. It really does make you start to hate the heat.
context: Reply to a commenter who said late pregnancy in summer made her hate summer.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: It almost feels like you’re trapped in your own body and can’t really do the things you want anymore. You don’t feel free, and I think that’s the hardest part.
context: Overdue, replying to advice to enjoy the last days.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: constantly worrying about doing everything right and not making any mistakes has been mentally exhausting.
context: Says the pregnancy itself was not hard; the vigilance was.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: i just wish I could have had a normal pregnancy. I feel like I can’t get anything done because I am constantly hyper aware and on edge.
context: 35 weeks after a previous loss; repeated hospital checks for movement.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: My shifts are typically 11 hours, 5-6 days a week. I have two back to back scheduled Saturdays coming up, so that’s 66+ hour work weeks for two weeks straight.
context: 17 weeks, four months into a new job, sick most of the pregnancy.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: My partner, who works for the company, just in a different building, said it ‘won’t end well’ if I turn them in
context: Her doctor wrote a 40-hour weekly limit; she is afraid to hand it to her employer.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m told if I turn in these work restrictions it’ll be like spitting in the manager’s face who has helped me so much (my partner told me this).
context: Partner discouraging her from submitting doctor's hour limits.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I dread every day at work because who knows how sick I’ll be. How tired I’ll be. And there’s no end in sight to my work weeks except for one day to ‘recover’.
context: Long shifts while sick at 17 weeks.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I saw a prenatal chiropractor who told me my hips are uneven and my pelvis is tilted. I've had adjustments, but they haven't provided any meaningful relief.
context: 29 weeks, severe groin and hip pain that keeps her in bed.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I'm not looking for generic advice like "take Tylenol and rest." I've done all of that.
context: Asking strangers what actually helped similar pain.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I am currently seeing a pelvic floor PT twice a week and she has worked WONDERS on me. I'm in absolute awe. She knew what to do the second I walked in!!
context: Follow-up nearly four weeks later, at almost 33 weeks.
